text: >> Every spring common loons come back to the Whitefish chain in Minnesota. >>  >> They nest a few feet from the water because a loon can barely walk. >>  >> They dive for fish they have to see, so clear water matters. And every fall they need a quarter mile of open lake to get airborne.  One bad choice at any of those moments and the year is lost. >>  >> Loon Nest is a humanitarian's AI project that turns that year into something you  can play. Four short browser games, each about a minute. In Nest Site, you pick where the nest goes. Too high and the bird cannot

Reach it. >>  >> Too low and a boat wake swamps it. Deep Dive, you feed chicks as the water clouds over.  Put lead tackle as the hazard in Chick Taxi. The youngest players carry chicks on a parent's back. In Runway, you build speed across open water for  the one takeoff that matters. Behind the games is fieldwork. Northeastern graduate volunteers fly drones over the lake, turn  the footage into an annotated data set, build tools for spotting and counting loons at the National Loon Center in Crosslake and keeping  use. We are not loon experts. That is the point. The games get built,
the biologist correct, and the corrections make the next version truer. Play  them at loon. documentarians.ai Nothing to install. >>
